clue.text: Communications from dining room taking a long time

indicators.note: the dining room takes on the long time, so one word is followed by the other

parts.note: a mess is a dining room for members of the armed forces
'ages' is everyday speech for a long time

explanation.surface: Messages sent out from the officers' dining room take forever to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages are communications: notes, texts or letters passed from one person to another.

clue.text: Error discovered by end of term, I wager

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of the word term

parts.note: a stake is the money wagered on a bet

explanation.surface: A gambler bets that a mistake will come to light by the end of the school term.
explanation.definitionFit: An error and a mistake are straightforward synonyms for something done wrongly.

clue.text: Take off sports gear

definitions.meaning: to remove clothing or a covering, as in undressing
a team's kit of shirts and shorts, as in the club's away colours

explanation.surface: An instruction to a player to remove their kit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for undressing and the noun for a team's playing kit, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Cook I mess about, not eating or drinking a lot

definitions.text: not eating or drinking a lot

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the following letters are doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef admits to fooling around in the kitchen while hardly eating or drinking himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a noun addressed by name, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange I MESS ABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstemious is moderate and self-denying, especially in food and alcohol.

clue.text: Number of team members: one seen after another?

definitions.meaning: a football or cricket side has this many players
write the figure 1 and then another 1 beside it and the figures read as this number

explanation.surface: Counting the players in a side, one after the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is cryptic: the digit one placed after another one gives 11.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket teams both field a side of this many players, so the number is used for the team itself.

clue.text: Softy starts to whine, ignoring manly pursuits

indicators.note: the starts of the following four words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A weakling whines and stays away from macho activities.
explanation.definitionFit: A softy is a weak, timid person, and a wimp is the informal word for such a feeble character.

clue.text: Animosity expressed by ailing Bard

parts.note: someone ailing is sick or unwell
the Bard is Shakespeare, whose first name was William, shortened to Will

explanation.surface: A sickly Shakespeare voices his hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is the usual nickname for William Shakespeare, here as plain Will.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is hostility or resentment, which the two-word phrase for bad feeling towards someone describes.

clue.text: Spike Milligan's last seen in short programme

indicators.note: the letter is seen within the shortened word, so it sits inside it
short tells you to cut the word programme down to its familiar clipped form
the last of Milligan is its closing letter

explanation.surface: Spike Milligan's final appearance came in a brief show.
explanation.walkthrough: Spike Milligan was a British comedian of The Goon Show, so 'Spike' looks like his name, but it is the definition. PROG is the clipped form of programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a spike, such as one of the pointed tines of a fork.

clue.text: Brought back puddings, under pressure

indicators.note: bringing a word back means writing it in the other direction

parts.note: puddings is the British word for desserts, the sweet course

explanation.surface: A cook, harried and anxious, serves the sweet course again.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means being anxious and strained, which is how someone under pressure feels.

clue.text: Voice that has changed a lot

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase have been changed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer's voice has altered greatly, as when a boy's voice breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singing voice, the lowest female or highest adult male range.

clue.text: Give weapons to old fellow for final battle

parts.note: to arm someone is to equip them with weapons
aged means old
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: Handing arms to an elderly man ahead of the last great fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the last battle between good and evil foretold in the Book of Revelation.

clue.text: Head leaving specimen that's more than enough

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, goes away

parts.note: a sample is a specimen taken for testing

explanation.surface: A lab specimen is plentiful once the head has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, enough or more than enough for the need.

clue.text: Wrong about a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: the word for wrong goes about, around, the letter A

parts.note: erring means being in the wrong, making a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken about an item of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An earring is a piece of jewellery worn on the ear lobe.

clue.text: Bring about English translation of Latin

indicators.note: translating here means moving the letters of the word into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Turning a Latin text into English brings about a result.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or necessitate something as a consequence, that is, to cause it.

clue.text: Turncoat's first motive for disloyalty

indicators.note: the first of the word turncoat is its opening letter

parts.note: a reason is a motive for doing something

explanation.surface: A defector's main reason for betraying his side.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the crime of betraying one's country, the gravest kind of disloyalty.

clue.text: Daddy and girl displaying Spanish dish

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A father and daughter show off a dish from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish from Valencia, cooked with saffron, seafood or chicken.

clue.text: Lose oar tossed about in spray

indicators.note: letters tossed about land in a jumbled new order

explanation.surface: A rower drops an oar that is thrown around in the sea spray.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a can that releases its contents as a fine mist or spray.

clue.text: Go for garage job?

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is a formal way of saying to go there
a mending job done on a car at a garage

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to take on a job at the local garage.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense, as in 'repair to the drawing room', is formal and old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to go somewhere and the mending work a mechanic does, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Put to death in river? Charming!

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
cute means charming or appealing

explanation.surface: Someone is drowned as punishment in a river, and a bystander remarks sarcastically on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England, flowing through Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute someone is to carry out a sentence of death on them.

clue.text: Joint that's associated with grease

definitions.meaning: the hinge in the middle of the arm
the phrase completed by grease means hard physical work

explanation.surface: A joint that needs oiling.
explanation.walkthrough: Elbow grease is an idiom for hard physical effort, such as scrubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the joint between the upper arm and forearm; it also pairs with grease in the idiom for hard work.

clue.text: Key buried by Aberdeen terrier

indicators.note: the letters are buried within the words, concealed across them

explanation.surface: A Scottish dog has buried a key.
explanation.definitionFit: Enter is the key on a computer keyboard that confirms an input.

clue.text: Principle unaffected by revolution

definitions.note: a core belief of a creed, and that word reads identically from either end

indicators.note: turning the word round end to end leaves it exactly as it was

parts.note: a core belief of a creed, and that word reads identically from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that survives political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' suggests political overthrow but here means turning the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or belief held as true, especially by a group.

clue.text: Hit graduates hard

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Students who have just graduated strike hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To bash is to hit something hard.

clue.text: Astaire regularly eats fish

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one, from the name

parts.note: to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: The dancer Fred Astaire routinely eats fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardines are small oily fish, often sold tinned.

clue.text: Decline a new mobile

indicators.note: mobile letters move around, ending in a new order

explanation.surface: Sales of a newly launched mobile phone fall off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile' looks like a phone, but it signals moving the letters of A NEW about.
explanation.definitionFit: To wane is to decline or dwindle, as the moon does after it is full.

clue.text: Parental correction before birth

indicators.note: correcting the letters of the word puts them into a different order

explanation.surface: Parents discipline their child even before it is born.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenatal means occurring before birth, as in care given during pregnancy.
